- **`Edge`** — One connection between two nodes, and the verdict that selects it.
- **`Graph`** — A mutable graph. Edits mutate it; serialization canonicalizes it.
- **`Invariant`** — A mode-declared rule, for the parts only the author can know.
- **`Knob`** — A declared parameter: a default, a kind, and optional bounds.
- **`Memory`** — A namespace a mode may keep, with the policy that governs its life.
- **`Mode`** — Base class for a mode. Subclasses declare knobs, build, score.
- **`Node`** — One step of a mode.
- **`Package`** — A named collection of modes, plus the operation modules they call.
- **`Port`** — Something a run publishes, so a reader knows what it has rather than guessing.

<a id="refactory_dsh-nn-edits"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.nn.edits`

The edit algebra: every structural change is typed data.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `EditError` | `(message: 'str', code: 'str' = 'E-shape') -> 'None'` |
| class | `EditSpec` | `(name: 'str', kind: 'str', description: 'str', fields: 'tuple[str, ...]', macro: 'bool' = False, precondition: 'Callable[[dict, State], str \| None] \| None' = None, expand: 'Callable[[dict, State], list[dict]] \| None' = None, apply: 'Callable[[State, dict], State] \| None' = None) -> None` |
| function | `apply` | `(edit: 'dict', state: 'Mapping[str, Any]') -> 'State'` |
| function | `apply_many` | `(edits: 'Iterable[dict]', state: 'Mapping[str, Any]') -> 'State'` |
| function | `catalogue` | `(preset: 'str' = 'broad') -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `configure` | `(state: 'Mapping[str, Any]', name: 'str', value: 'Any') -> 'State'` |
| function | `enabled` | `(preset: 'str' = 'broad') -> 'list[str]'` |
| function | `is_macro` | `(name: 'str') -> 'bool'` |
| function | `names` | `() -> 'list[str]'` |
| function | `precheck` | `(edit: 'dict', state: 'Mapping[str, Any]') -> 'str \| None'` |
| function | `random_edit` | `(state: 'Mapping[str, Any]', *, preset: 'str' = 'broad', insertable: 'Sequence[Any]' = (), rng: 'random.Random \| None' = None) -> 'dict \| None'` |
| function | `unknown` | `(op: 'object') -> 'str \| None'` |

- **`EditError`** — An edit cannot be applied to this state. The state is left untouched.
- **`EditSpec`** — One operation in the catalogue.
- **`apply`** — Apply ``edit`` and return a new state, leaving ``state`` untouched.
- **`catalogue`** — The enabled operations, described for an optimizer's prompt.
- **`configure`** — Set a knob for the run being made, refusing a bad name or value but not a freeze.
- **`enabled`** — The operations a preset allows. An unknown preset is an error.
- **`precheck`** — The reason ``edit`` cannot be applied, for the checks that need no state.
- **`random_edit`** — A random edit from the enabled set, or ``None`` if none can be built.
- **`unknown`** — The refusal for an op the catalogue does not have, or None when it does.

- **`Invariant`** — A mode-declared rule, for the parts only the author can know.
- **`Issue`** — One reason a state was refused.
- **`artifact_produced`** — Keep a named artifact producer in the executable graph during search.
- **`declared_knobs`** — The knobs a state declares, as ``Knob`` objects.
- **`fact_produced`** — An invariant requiring the graph to produce the facts ``score()`` reads.
- **`on_path_nodes`** — Nodes that lie on some ``start -> terminal`` path.
- **`produced_on_path`** — Every write and fact produced by a node on a ``start -> terminal`` path.
- **`rules_text`** — The rules, as the optimizer prompt shows them.
- **`validate`** — Every reason ``(graph, values)`` is not a runnable, scoreable mode.
- **`validate_state`** — Validate a state dict without building a mode around it.

<a id="refactory_dsh-optim-policies"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.optim.policies`

Optimizers whose distinguishing choice is *which parent* to breed from.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `ArchiveSelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0, limit: 'int' = 12) -> 'None'` |
| class | `EvolutionarySelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0, tournament: 'int' = 3) -> 'None'` |
| class | `HillClimbSelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'None'` |
| class | `IslandsSelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0, count: 'int' = 3) -> 'None'` |
| class | `MapElitesSelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0, explore: 'float' = 0.3) -> 'None'` |
| class | `ParentSelector` | `(*, k: 'int' = 3, seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'None'` |

- **`ArchiveSelector`** — SRF `scs`: breed from the best of everything seen, not just this epoch.
- **`EvolutionarySelector`** — SRF `evox`: a tournament, so a weaker member can still breed.
- **`HillClimbSelector`** — SRF `karpathy`: one candidate per round, from the best so far.
- **`IslandsSelector`** — SRF `openevolve`: sub-populations whose lineages never cross.
- **`MapElitesSelector`** — SRF's own optimizer (`srf/lab/map_elites.py`): a champion per niche.
- **`ParentSelector`** — An optimizer that chooses parents by a policy, then samples an edit for each.

<a id="refactory_dsh-steering"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.steering`

Steering a run while *using* it: the intent ledger, and the transform that adds it.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `Ledger` | `(root: 'Path') -> 'None'` |
| class | `SteeringError` | `` |
| function | `annotate` | `(workflow: 'Any', ledger: 'Ledger') -> 'Any'` |
| function | `chain` | `(ledger: 'Ledger', outputs: 'Mapping[str, str]', *, deliveries: 'Mapping[str, Any] \| None' = None, completed_nodes: 'frozenset[str] \| set[str] \| None' = None) -> 'list[str]'` |
| function | `citations` | `(text: 'str') -> 'list[str]'` |
| function | `fidelity` | `(ledger: 'Ledger', outputs: 'Mapping[str, str] \| None' = None, *, deliveries: 'Mapping[str, Any] \| None' = None, completed_nodes: 'frozenset[str] \| set[str] \| None' = None) -> 'list[str]'` |
| function | `for_run` | `(workflow: 'Any', workdir: 'Path') -> 'Any'` |
| function | `interactive` | `(state: 'dict[str, Any]', workdir: 'Path', *, request: 'str' = '', name: 'str' = '', description: 'str' = '') -> 'tuple[Any, Ledger]'` |
| function | `outputs_in` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, str]'` |
| function | `strip_steering` | `(text: 'str') -> 'str'` |

- **`Ledger`** — The run's record of what was asked for, and everything said since.
- **`SteeringError`** — The steering layer cannot be built or trusted. Always names what is wrong.
- **`annotate`** — Fold the ledger into every agent node. A no-op when the ledger is empty.
- **`chain`** — Problems with the chain from the ledger to the work, mechanically.
- **`citations`** — The ledger entries a piece of work says it serves, in the order it names them.
- **`fidelity`** — What is wrong with a ledger a run is about to be judged against.
- **`for_run`** — Fold the run directory's ledger into a workflow about to run.
- **`interactive`** — Lower a mode for a person to *use*, with the steering layer attached.
- **`outputs_in`** — What each agent node wrote, read back so the citation chain can be checked.
- **`strip_steering`** — Remove the STEERING_START/STEERING_END block from a prompt string.

- **`AdaptiveMeta`** — SRF `adaevolve`: an adaptive meta-level.
- **`Archive`** — A set of candidates a strategy keeps, and how it picks from them.
- **`Autoscientists`** — SRF `autoscientists`: `Fork(N scientists) → Join → merge`.
- **`BestOfN`** — SRF `best_of_n`: `Fork(N samples) → Join → select_best`.
- **`FlatArchive`** — Keeps everything. The default loop's behaviour.
- **`Reflective`** — SRF `gepa`: reflective evolution, with a merge branch.
- **`ReflectiveSampler`** — SRF `shinka`: reflection inside sampling.
- **`ResearchThenOptimize`** — SRF `autoresearch`: a pre-phase, then the loop.
- **`StagedCurriculum`** — SRF `ai_sci_v2`: a staged curriculum, not a loop.
- **`StagedV1`** — SRF `ai_sci_v1`: the earlier staged variant.
- **`TreeArchive`** — A tree. A node's parent is the node it was expanded from.
- **`TreeSearch`** — SRF `aide`: `policy → action_gate(draft|improve|debug) → tree_update`.
- **`create`** — Build a strategy by name, failing loud on an unknown one.
- **`register`** — Add a strategy without editing the library.

- **`EpochSummary`** — One epoch, as the report and the scheduler describe it.
- **`Loop`** — The default outer loop: the eight steps over one mode.
- **`LoopConfig`** — How a run is shaped.
- **`LoopError`** — The run cannot proceed. Always names what is wrong with the mode.
- **`main`** — ``python -m refactory_dsh.loop <package>/<mode> [options]``.
- **`node_count`** — How many nodes a candidate's graph holds, which is what the size cost counts.
- **`run`** — Build a loop and run it to its bound.

- **`AgentNode`** — Node that invokes an agent.
- **`ArtifactCheck`** — Validation rule for an agent-produced artifact.
- **`DataItem`** — Standardized data payload for per-item workflow iteration.
- **`DataNode`** — Node that loads data items and drives per-item execution of a subgraph.
- **`FnNode`** — Node that runs a deterministic shell command or Python callable.
- **`ForkNode`** — Parallel execution node that launches all targets concurrently.
- **`GateNode`** — Decision node that produces a verdict.
- **`JoinNode`** — Barrier node that waits for all sources to complete.
- **`Node`** — Base node in the workflow graph, with v2 extension fields.
- **`Workflow`** — A directed graph of typed nodes with labeled edges.

- **`PackageClash`** — A package name exists in both the install and the workspace.
- **`add`** — Copy a package into the workspace, refusing a clash.
- **`catalogue`** — Modes grouped by package: the only way they are ever listed.
- **`describe_mode`** — One mode's surface, for a person about to optimize it or read a report.
- **`discover`** — Every package that loads. A package that fails to import is reported.
- **`discover_names`** — Every package directory, installed or in the workspace.
- **`import_package`** — Bring a package in from a path or a git URL.
- **`install_workspace`** — Make workspace packages importable under `refactory_packages`.
- **`installed_names`** — Package directories on disk, enabled or not.

- **`main`** — ``python -m refactory_dsh.registry list | show <mode>``.
- **`missing_tools`** — The names of required tools this machine does not have, for a listing.
- **`packages_root`** — The directory holding every package.
- **`provenance`** — Where a package came from, as the writer recorded it.
- **`remove`** — Delete a workspace package, refusing to break a dependent.
- **`render_catalogue`** — The grouped listing a user sees.
- **`resolve`** — The package and mode class for ``<package>/<name>``.
- **`smoke`** — Run one mode once, so a package can be checked rather than merely imported.
- **`tool_report`** — Every declared tool of every package, with its status on this machine.
- **`tools`** — The tools a package declares, read without importing it.
- **`verify`** — Import every mode of a package and say what is wrong with it.
- **`where`** — Which root a package lives in, or ``None`` if it is not there.
- **`workspace_root`** — The writable package root for a project.

- **`Tool`** — One thing a package needs that is not a Python callable.

- **`ToolMissing`** — A tool a package declared is not present on this machine.
- **`ToolStatus`** — Whether one declared tool is present, and what was found.
- **`ToolchainError`** — A tool declaration is malformed, or a declared tool is not usable here.
- **`absent`** — The ones this machine does not have.
- **`check`** — Probe every declared tool, present or not.
- **`import_tool`** — The module a ``python`` tool declares, imported, or the missing-tool error.
- **`preflight`** — Every required tool a package declares, or the error listing what is missing.
- **`probe`** — Whether one declared tool is usable here, and what was found.
- **`read_tools`** — What a package declares it needs. Empty when it declares nothing.
- **`report`** — Every tool a package declares, with its status on this machine.
- **`require`** — One tool a node is about to use, or :class:`ToolMissing` naming the fix.
- **`tool_env`** — The environment a package's *present* tools need, for a run elsewhere.

- **`SandboxError`** — A sandboxed run could not be carried out.
- **`SandboxResult`** — What a sandboxed run produced.
- **`ast_check`** — Everything wrong with a package that can be seen without importing it.
- **`describe_package`** — A package's manifest and mode ids, read without importing it here.
- **`is_secret`** — Whether an environment name looks like a credential, which a sandboxed run never sees.
- **`is_signal_crash`** — Whether a sandbox result is a signal crash that survived run_command's retry.
- **`main`** — ``python -m refactory_dsh.sandbox --ast <pkg> | --smoke <pkg>/<mode>``.
- **`missing_init`** — Why a package root has no `__init__.py`, and what it holds instead.
- **`model_readiness`** — Check the model path after the same scrub/HOME rewrite as real smoke.
- **`promote`** — Mark a package trusted, explicitly, and record who did it.
- **`refactory_env`** — ``scrub(env)`` with refactory's own interpreter first on PATH.
- **`run_command`** — Run a shell command in the sandbox, bounded by time rather than memory.
- **`run_sandboxed`** — Run a snippet in a subprocess with limits, from the workspace, scrubbed.
- **`scrub`** — The environment a sandboxed run sees: an allowlist, with secrets dropped.
- **`smoke`** — Run one mode once, in a sandbox, and report what it scored.
- **`usage`** — The one usage line, printed both for ``--help`` and for misuse.
- **`verify_sandboxed`** — Everything wrong with a package, checked without importing it here.

- **`main`** — ``python -m refactory_dsh.create --name <n> --brief <text> [--extends <mode>]``.
- **`parse_verdicts`** — The gate verdicts a headless authoring run was given, as ``gate=value``.
- **`result_from_run`** — The facts of a create-mode run, for a caller that drove the executor itself.

<a id="refactory_dsh-repo_change"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.repo_change`

The steps a mode uses to change a repository: where it works, what lands, how it is checked.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| function | `apply_emission` | `(answer: 'str', found: 'worktree.Worktree', workdir: 'Path', *, from_worktree: 'bool' = False) -> 'tuple[dict[Path, str], tuple[Path, ...], str, list[str]]'` |
| function | `knob_names` | `() -> 'tuple[str, ...]'` |
| function | `knobs` | `() -> 'dict[str, Knob]'` |
| function | `locate` | `(ctx: 'Any', name: 'str', task: 'dict[str, Any]', *, in_worktree: 'bool \| None' = None, needs_worktree: 'tuple[str, ...]' = (), output_only: 'tuple[str, ...]' = ()) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `materialise` | `(ctx: 'Any', *, source: 'Path \| None' = None, files: 'tuple[str, ...]' = ()) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `materialise_node` | `(**fields: 'Any') -> 'Node'` |
| function | `prepare_check_environment` | `(found: 'worktree.Worktree', facts: 'dict[str, Any]', *, amend: 'bool', commit_lockfiles: 'bool', run: 'Path', home: 'Path', timeout: 'float', budget: 'Any' = None) -> 'tuple[worktree.Worktree, dict[str, str], list[str], dict[str, Any] \| None]'` |
| function | `prepare_commands` | `(ctx: 'Any', found: 'worktree.Worktree', env: 'dict[str, str]', home: 'Path', timeout: 'float', budget: 'Any', *, amend: 'bool' = True) -> 'tuple[worktree.Worktree, list[str], dict[str, Any] \| None]'` |
| function | `produces` | `() -> 'tuple[str, ...]'` |
| function | `refuse_truncated` | `(path: 'Path', text: 'str') -> 'None'` |
| function | `refused` | `(ctx: 'Any') -> 'str'` |
| function | `report` | `(ctx: 'Any', name: 'str', payload: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `run_check` | `(ctx: 'Any', command: 'str', timeout: 'float', *, triage_prep: 'bool' = True) -> 'Any'` |
| function | `wants_worktree` | `(ctx: 'Any') -> 'bool'` |

- **`apply_emission`** — Parse emit.txt and resolve edits against the run worktree, read-only.
- **`knob_names`** — The knobs `knobs` declares, for the prepare node's ``knobs``.
- **`knobs`** — The knobs that say where a run works.
- **`locate`** — Where the run works, as facts for the mode's prepare op to return.
- **`materialise`** — Make the emitted files the run's artifact: a commit in its worktree, when it has one.
- **`materialise_node`** — The op that applies ``emit.txt`` as the run's next attempt (`materialise`).
- **`prepare_check_environment`** — Install dependencies, build check environment, run generate/setup.
- **`prepare_commands`** — Run the run's generate command, then its setup command, in a prepared worktree.
- **`produces`** — The facts `locate` returns, for the prepare node's ``produces``.
- **`refuse_truncated`** — Refuse text copied from a read that the read tool cut short, before it is written anywhere.
- **`refused`** — Why `materialise` could not apply the last ``emit.txt``; empty when it did.
- **`report`** — Settle the run's place, write the mode's report ``name`` from ``payload``, and return it.
- **`run_check`** — Run ``command`` where the run works, and return its `sandbox.SandboxResult`.
- **`wants_worktree`** — Whether the run's ``worktree`` knob asks for a worktree, as it does unless turned off.


<a id="refactory_dsh-observe"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.observe`

What a reader needs to show a run: progress while it happens, a diff of a

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| function | `artifact_manifest` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `candidate_diff` | `(run_root: 'Path', candidate_id: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `diff_states` | `(before: 'dict[str, Any]', after: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `graph_summary` | `(state: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'str'` |
| function | `progress` | `(run_root: 'Path', *, after: 'int' = 0) -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `render_diff` | `(diff: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'str'` |

- **`artifact_manifest`** — The run's readable outputs, for a reader that knows nothing about the loop.
- **`candidate_diff`** — A candidate's state against its parent's, as the run left them on disk.
- **`diff_states`** — What changed between two mode states: knobs, nodes, and edges.
- **`graph_summary`** — The graph's size, so a reader can size up a candidate without loading it.
- **`progress`** — Every step recorded since line ``after``, so a reader can tail the run.
- **`render_diff`** — The diff as markdown, for the report and for a reader.


<a id="refactory_dsh-cli"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.cli`

The one command: `refactory`.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| function | `build_parser` | `() -> 'argparse.ArgumentParser'` |
| function | `cmd_ceo` | `(args: 'argparse.Namespace') -> 'int'` |
| function | `cmd_doctor` | `(args: 'argparse.Namespace') -> 'int'` |
| function | `cmd_list` | `(args: 'argparse.Namespace') -> 'int'` |
| function | `cmd_ui` | `(args: 'argparse.Namespace') -> 'int'` |
| function | `main` | `(argv: 'list[str] \| None' = None) -> 'int'` |
| function | `slug` | `(text: 'str', *, words: 'int' = 3) -> 'str'` |

- **`build_parser`** — The command line, with one verb per question a person has.
- **`cmd_ceo`** — Describe what you want: an authoring mode, or a mode to run.
- **`cmd_doctor`** — Whether this machine can run a mode, and what to do about anything missing.
- **`cmd_list`** — What this checkout can do.
- **`cmd_ui`** — The GUI, launched from this checkout (the panel and the tool both live here).
- **`main`** — Dispatch one verb onto the module that owns it.
- **`slug`** — A name for what was asked for, when the asker did not give one.


<a id="refactory_dsh-console"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.console`

Driving a run from a GUI: the catalogue, a live run, and what it produced.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `ConsoleError` | `` |
| function | `artifacts` | `(run_root: 'Path', *, contents: 'bool' = False) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `candidate` | `(run_root: 'Path', candidate_id: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `catalogue` | `(*, project: 'Path \| None' = None) -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `comparison` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `gates` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `holdout` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, Any] \| None'` |
| function | `leaderboard` | `(run_root: 'Path', *, limit: 'int' = 20) -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `level_two` | `() -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `list_projects` | `() -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `main` | `(argv: 'list[str] \| None' = None) -> 'int'` |
| function | `runs` | `(*, project: 'Path \| None' = None, runs_root: 'Path \| None' = None, limit: 'int' = 20) -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `runtime_context` | `(project: 'Path', *, provider: 'str' = '', model: 'str' = '') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `start` | `(mode: 'str', *, project: 'Path \| None' = None, runs_root: 'Path \| None' = None, run_id: 'str \| None' = None, **config: 'Any') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `status` | `(run_root: 'Path', *, after: 'int' = 0) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `stop` | `(run_root: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |

- **`ConsoleError`** — The request cannot be served, and why.
- **`artifacts`** — What the run left, and — when asked — what is in it.
- **`candidate`** — One candidate, with what it changed against the parent it came from.
- **`catalogue`** — Every mode a run can be started from, with the surface it exposes.
- **`comparison`** — Compare measured and unmeasured states without promoting missing metrics.
- **`gates`** — The `user` gates this run is stopped at, and the verdicts each accepts.
- **`holdout`** — The held-out audit a run recorded, or ``None`` when it recorded none.
- **`leaderboard`** — The candidates by score, with each one's diff against its parent.
- **`level_two`** — The three level-2 seams by name, each with what it says it is.
- **`list_projects`** — The registered projects, as the GUI's target picker needs them.
- **`runs`** — Every run under the root, newest first, each with where it got to.
- **`runtime_context`** — Describe the existing nested model configuration without a model request.
- **`start`** — Begin a run in its own process, and hand back the id to watch it with.
- **`status`** — Where the run is, and what is new since the reader last looked.
- **`stop`** — Ask the run to stop, and say whether it did.

<a id="refactory_dsh-workers"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.workers`

Worker routes and durable receipts over DSH's named-provider registry.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `GraphTelemetry` | `(workdir: 'Path', context: 'dict[str, Any]', budget: 'Any' = None)` |
| function | `account_usage` | `(budget: 'Any', receipt: 'dict[str, Any]', *, final: 'bool' = False) -> 'None'` |
| function | `begin` | `(workdir: 'Path', route: 'dict[str, Any]', *, node: 'str' = '', role: 'str' = 'worker') -> 'Path'` |
| function | `capabilities` | `(backend: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `environment` | `(context: 'dict[str, Any] \| None') -> 'dict[str, str]'` |
| function | `event` | `(workdir: 'Path', record: 'dict[str, Any]', state: 'str', summary: 'str') -> 'None'` |
| function | `finish` | `(path: 'Path', state: 'str', *, error: 'str \| None' = None) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `lower_workflow` | `(workflow: 'Any', workdir: 'Path', model_context: 'dict[str, Any] \| None', declarations: 'dict[str, Any] \| None' = None) -> 'Any'` |
| function | `now` | `() -> 'str'` |
| function | `observer_patch` | `(path: 'Path', route: 'dict[str, Any]', provider_config: 'dict[str, Any] \| None' = None) -> 'None'` |
| function | `permission_patch` | `(route: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `provider_rows` | `(route: 'dict[str, Any]', provider_config: 'dict[str, Any] \| None') -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `resolve_route` | `(base: 'dict[str, Any]', *, role: 'str' = 'worker', node: 'str' = '', role_routes: 'dict[str, Any] \| None' = None, node_routes: 'dict[str, Any] \| None' = None) -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `run_graph_command` | `(argv: 'list[str]', *, workdir: 'Path', context: 'dict[str, Any]', timeout: 'float \| None' = None, env: 'dict[str, str] \| None' = None, stop_condition: 'Any \| None' = None, **kwargs: 'Any') -> 'Any'` |
| function | `validate_route` | `(route: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `write_patch` | `(path: 'Path', runtime_root: 'Path', route: 'dict[str, Any]', provider_config: 'dict[str, Any] \| None' = None) -> 'None'` |

- **`GraphTelemetry`** — One coordinator receipt; node subprocesses own distinct worker receipts.
- **`account_usage`** — Keep measured DSH calls while exposing incomplete delegated coverage.
- **`environment`** — Nonsecret resolved context for graph-owned calls.
- **`lower_workflow`** — Resolve explicit node workers before graph dispatch, preserving all edges.
- **`permission_patch`** — Scope DSH bypass to this runtime, without leaking through child env.
- **`provider_rows`** — Declare selected provider routes to a runtime that cannot see profiles.
- **`resolve_route`** — Explicit node overrides role overrides run; runtime supplies empty fields.
- **`run_graph_command`** — Inherit terminal IO while polling graph resource and coordinator receipts.
- **`write_patch`** — Compose installed DSH services, never a parallel agent wire protocol.

<a id="refactory_dsh-items"></a>

## `refactory_dsh.items`

The per-item half of a data node, from the command line.

| kind | name | signature |
|---|---|---|
| class | `ItemsError` | `` |
| function | `command_begin` | `(node: 'Node', workdir: 'Path', index: 'int') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `command_end` | `(node: 'Node', workdir: 'Path', index: 'int') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `command_list` | `(node: 'Node', workdir: 'Path') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `command_reset` | `(workdir: 'Path', request: 'dict[str, Any]') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `data_node` | `(workdir: 'Path', node_id: 'str') -> 'Node'` |
| function | `items_of` | `(node: 'Node', workdir: 'Path') -> 'list[dict[str, Any]]'` |
| function | `main` | `(argv: 'list[str] \| None' = None) -> 'int'` |
| function | `source_override` | `(workdir: 'Path', node_id: 'str') -> 'dict[str, Any]'` |
| function | `write_source` | `(workdir: 'Path', *, source_path: 'str', source_format: 'str' = 'directory', node_id: 'str' = '*') -> 'Path'` |

- **`ItemsError`** — A data node cannot be iterated: named, because the node id alone is not a reason.
- **`command_begin`** — Materialise one item and prepare the workspace for its pass.
- **`command_end`** — The Task's verdict on one pass, folded into the run's facts.
- **`command_list`** — How many items the node iterates, and what they are called.
- **`command_reset`** — Archive prior facts, then invalidate the facts of explicitly redone work.
- **`data_node`** — The data node the declarations describe, as the graph language's own node.
- **`items_of`** — The data node's items, loaded the one way both runtimes load them.
- **`source_override`** — What this run says the data node should read, or an empty answer.
- **`write_source`** — Point a data node of this run at a source, before the graph starts.
